_COMMENT_FILE_PATH: SAVE THIS FILE AS: config_dryrun_futures.json — in the ROOT of your NostalgiaForInfinity repo (same folder as NostalgiaForInfinityX7.py, config_dryrun_telegram.json). NOT inside user_data/, NOT inside configs/.
_COMMENT_purpose: Dry-run only — no real orders are ever placed (dry_run: true). Runs the SAME strategy file (NostalgiaForInfinityX7.py) as config_dryrun_telegram.json, but with trading_mode=futures on OKX instead of spot on KuCoin, so the two can be compared side by side on the same strategy logic. The strategy auto-detects futures mode from trading_mode below (is_futures_mode / can_short) — no code changes needed.
_COMMENT_why_okx_not_binance: Binance Futures has the strongest official backtest numbers for this strategy, but its public API returns HTTP 451 (geo-blocked) from GitHub Actions runners (Azure US datacenters are inside Binance's 'Restricted Location' list per their Terms of Service) — confirmed via a live connectivity test, not assumed. Bybit is blocked the same way. OKX, Gate.io, and Kraken Futures were all confirmed reachable; OKX was chosen for its broader freqtrade support (e.g. stoploss_on_exchange works on both its spot and futures markets).
_COMMENT_separate_database: IMPORTANT: futures trades must never land in the same `trades` table as spot trades, or every stats/dashboard script that assumes one trading mode breaks. Instead of a second Supabase project, this reuses the SAME Supabase project/database as spot, but writes into a separate Postgres SCHEMA called `futures` (spot stays in the default `public` schema) — fully isolated tables, same project, same SUPABASE_DB_URL secret. The schema-selection happens in the workflow file (dry-run-telegram-futures.yml), not here, by appending ?options=-csearch_path=futures to the connection string at runtime. One-time setup required: run `CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS futures;` once in the Supabase SQL Editor before the first run.
_COMMENT_restart_architecture: Same self-queueing restart chain as the spot workflow — see dry-run-telegram-futures.yml for details. Open simulated trades survive restarts because db_url points at Postgres, not local SQLite.
_COMMENT_position_adjustment: NostalgiaForInfinityX7 requires position_adjustment_enable=true for its Grinding V2 and Buyback systems to function, in futures exactly as in spot.
_COMMENT_leverage: futures_mode_leverage (and its rebuy/grind variants) are set INSIDE the strategy file itself (NostalgiaForInfinityX7.py), not here — default is 3.0x. This config only turns futures mode on; it doesn't control the leverage multiplier.

exchange.name: okx
exchange._COMMENT_password: OKX's API requires a passphrase (the 'password' field) in addition to key/secret. Left empty here since dry-run never calls authenticated endpoints for real trading — only public market-data endpoints are used to simulate trades.

_COMMENT_pairlist: Same pairlist filter chain as the spot config (see its comment for the full rationale), with ONE required difference: both VolumePairList entries below have lookback_days=1 added. Without it, freqtrade fails at startup with 'Exchange OKX does not support dynamic whitelist in this configuration' — OKX's futures/swap ticker data doesn't expose quoteVolume in the live-ticker format VolumePairList defaults to, so it must be switched to candle-based ('advanced mode') volume calculation instead. Confirmed via an actual failed run's log, not assumed.
_COMMENT_telegram: Reuses the SAME Telegram bot/chat as the spot dry-run (same TELEGRAM_TOKEN / TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID secrets) — bot_name below is what distinguishes futures messages from spot ones in that same chat. token/chat_id below are dummy placeholders satisfying the config schema; real values come from FREQTRADE__TELEGRAM__TOKEN / FREQTRADE__TELEGRAM__CHAT_ID env vars.
_COMMENT_db_url: Real value injected via FREQTRADE__DB_URL env var, built at runtime in dry-run-telegram-futures.yml from the SAME SUPABASE_DB_URL secret spot uses, with ?options=-csearch_path=futures appended so it lands in the separate 'futures' schema (see _COMMENT_separate_database above). This placeholder (SQLite) is never actually used at runtime.
